proof_audit.v13-c05-first: Passed. A weakly preferred but strictly cheaper bundle contradicts relative local nonsatiation and budget optimality; a strictly preferred affordable bundle contradicts optimality directly. These distinct inequalities combine with complete profit ownership, balanced transfers, global profit maxima and nonnegative prices. Convexity is not needed. The own-bundle premise excludes the externality economy. A satiation witness in the peer shows why the weak cost step can fail without LNS.
proof_audit.v13-c05-separation: Passed. The interior-segment perturbation is inside the open set eventually. Nearest points in a noncompact closed convex set exist because a minimizing sequence can be restricted to a bounded ball. For a boundary origin, external points on the negative interior ray and their projections both tend to zero; a subsequence of unit normals converges to a nonzero vector. Each inequality holds for every set point before taking the same subsequence, so no illicit countable-point argument is needed. Strictness follows only for interior points.
proof_audit.v13-c05-second: Passed. Weak-order completeness orders two strictly better endpoints and convex weak upper contours then imply convex strict contours. LNS supplies target closure. The strict-contour sum need not be ambient-open; the downward resource set has a nonempty dense ambient interior and supplies the open side. Separation, downward closure and feasible target closure give nonnegative prices, global firm maxima, zero-value disposal, household upper-contour support and balanced ownership transfers. Equal-cost strict improvements remain possible. Convex cheaper-bundle approximation plus relative continuity excludes them under the stated extra hypothesis; no new existence theorem is inferred.
proof_audit.v13-c05-failures: Passed. Zero wealth and a free desirable good yield support without attained consumer demand; a different positive price implements the same target even though the cheaper-point sufficient condition fails. The discrete technology is a union of whole downward branches, not its convex hull. Direct branch optimization proves efficiency; firm support inequalities exclude every nonnegative nonzero price. The convexified improvement is outside every original branch.
proof_audit.v13-c05-aggregation: Passed. A small bilateral income transfer differentiates a constant aggregate within the product-open domain. Independent income coordinates force each derivative to equal one common vector; connected intervals permit integration. Budget exhaustion implies p·b=1 and p·a_i=0, not componentwise positivity of b on a bounded domain. One fixed-total slice cannot support the same inference. Subsistence demand is globally solved after shifting each feasible domain; the displayed representative family is a positive demand construction, not interpersonal welfare or general integrability.
proof_audit.v13-c05-arrow: Passed. The finite universal domain contains weak orders and preserves all outsider pair ties. Both auxiliary constructions transport almost to strong decisiveness; applying them reaches all six directions using exactly three alternatives, then all others through a hub. Minimal-coalition contraction has a strict c>b branch and a b>=c branch; the latter includes equality and still implies a>c. An empty decisive set contradicts unanimity. Finiteness supplies a minimal nonempty set, hence a singleton. Dictatorship constrains that voter’s strict comparisons only. Finite profile checks corroborate these steps; they do not enumerate all social welfare functions.
proof_audit.v13-c05-social: Passed. Positive-weight attained global maxima are Pareto efficient. Cauchy–Schwarz equality and the max-min resource lower bound establish the three optima globally, including boundary exclusion. Utility scale changes require inverse weight adjustments to preserve a weighted social order; utility origins can reverse max-min. Max-min can keep dominated ties. The odd single-peaked median proof counts peaks at least/at most the median, including repeats, so cross-side ties do not remove the strict majority; no strategic extension is claimed.

independent_oracle.invalid_domains: Actual calls reject booleans/inexact/nonfinite/oversized rationals, dimension errors, unaffordable or invalid budgets, incomplete ownership, malformed ballots/tie partitions, wrong median domains, unsupported social objectives, duplicate/nonfinite JSON and executable/malformed numeric markers. These are peer-oracle checks; they are not represented as independent executions of the author’s input validator.
independent_oracle.limitations: Finite certificates do not prove the universal theorems, select a welfare criterion, demonstrate legal implementation, or validate real voting/income behavior. Those distinctions are retained in the prose review.
